hero.angle: Lead with the new manslaughter charge against Jabari Cowart after a BB gun shooting turned fatal in Fort Pierce, detailing the escalation from a group shooting BB guns at trees to a fatal shot and the victim's death at Lawnwood Hospital.

hero.body:
A 34-year-old Fort Pierce man died Saturday after being shot with a BB gun in the area of Avenue G, and the suspect has been charged with manslaughter. Fort Pierce Police Department officers responded to reports of a person suffering from a gunshot wound.

The investigation revealed that a group of men had been shooting BB guns at trees when the suspect, identified as Jabari Cowart, asked to use one of the BB guns. Cowart allegedly pointed the BB gun in the victim's direction and fired. Shortly afterward, the victim collapsed.

The victim was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died from his injuries. Police said Cowart was charged with manslaughter and taken to the St. Lucie County jail.

The case remains under investigation by the Fort Pierce Police Department.
hero.headline: Fort Pierce man dies after BB gun shooting, suspect charged with manslaughter

cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man faces a manslaughter charge after a 34-year-old man died from injuries sustained in a BB gun shooting Saturday in Fort Pierce. Jabari Cowart was charged with manslaughter and taken to the St. Lucie County jail following the fatal shooting in the area of Avenue G, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

The incident began when a group of men had been shooting BB guns at trees. Cowart asked to use one of the BB guns, then allegedly pointed the weapon in the victim's direction and fired, police said. The victim collapsed shortly afterward.

The victim was transported to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he later died from his injuries. The Fort Pierce Police Department responded to the area of Avenue G after receiving reports of a person suffering from a gunshot wound.

The case remains under investigation by the Fort Pierce Police Department. Police have not released the name of the victim.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed an EF0 landspout tornado touched down Sunday evening in St. Lucie County, damaging about 20 to 30 homes along a 2.1-mile path. Will Ulrich, warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service Melbourne office, announced the findings Monday morning during a press conference at Jessica Clinton Park following a damage survey conducted jointly with the City of Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management. No injuries were reported from the tornado, officials confirmed.

The tornado first touched down around 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitching Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, close to the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club, producing minimal structural damage including roof damage, soffit damage and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations. It then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout for approximately five to seven minutes before moving back onshore in the Bay St. Lucie community around 6:20 p.m. The strongest wind gusts likely occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, where the tornado caused numerous downed trees and large branches, along with damage to well-built homes with tile roofs from winds of 65 to 75 mph, Ulrich said.

The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, where it caused discontinuous damage including downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. The entire event lasted approximately 14 to 15 minutes, making it unusually long for this type of tornado. Most of the damage was classified as minor, with approximately 20 to 30 percent of roof covers removed from some homes, though no homes were destroyed. The National Weather Service worked alongside city and county emergency management to conduct interviews with residents and piece together the timeline of the event.
hero.headline: National Weather Service confirms EF0 tornado damaged 20 to 30 homes in Port St. Lucie

shadow.final_hero_headline: Sheriff's helicopter spots massive barn fire on Southwest Martin Highway in Palm City

hero.angle: Martin County Fire Rescue battled a 1,600-square-foot barn fire on Southwest Martin Highway in Palm City, spotted by a Sheriff's helicopter Sunday night; a motorhome and Jeep were destroyed inside, no injuries reported, and the State Fire Marshal is investigating the cause.

hero.body:
A Martin County Sheriff's Office helicopter flying over Palm City on Sunday night spotted a barn engulfed in flames on Southwest Martin Highway. Martin County Fire Rescue crews responded to the scene, where they found a 1,600-square-foot barn fully involved in fire with its roof already gone by the time they arrived.

Firefighters entered the structure and discovered a Class C motorhome and a Jeep inside the burning barn. Crews worked to extinguish the flames throughout the building and continued monitoring hot spots to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

Officials reported that no one was injured in the incident. Firefighters successfully contained the blaze and prevented it from spreading beyond the barn to surrounding areas or structures.

The State Fire Marshal was notified about the fire. The cause of the blaze remains under investigation, and no further details about what may have started the fire have been released at this time.
hero.headline: Sheriff's helicopter spots massive barn fire on Southwest Martin Highway in Palm City

hero.body:
Martin County Fire Rescue crews battled a 1,600-square-foot barn fire on Southwest Martin Highway in Palm City Sunday night after a Martin County Sheriff's Office helicopter flying over the area spotted the blaze. Firefighters arrived to find the barn engulfed in flames with its roof already gone. A Class C motorhome and a Jeep inside the structure were destroyed. No injuries were reported, and crews contained the fire before it spread beyond the barn.

The Sheriff's Office helicopter crew alerted authorities to the fire Sunday night. When Martin County Fire Rescue crews arrived at the Southwest Martin Highway location, the barn was already heavily damaged. Firefighters entered the structure and discovered the motorhome and Jeep inside.

Crews worked to extinguish the flames and monitored hot spots throughout the scene. Officials said firefighters successfully prevented the blaze from spreading to surrounding areas. The barn was a total loss.

The State Fire Marshal was notified of the incident. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Martin County Fire Rescue has not released further information about the property or circumstances surrounding the blaze.

cards.body:
Port St. Lucie residents in the Southbend Boulevard and Southeast Navy Ave neighborhood began cleanup efforts Monday after a possible tornado or landspout struck Sunday evening. Aaron Christiansen said he was home around 6 p.m. when he noticed something strange through his window and had about 10 seconds to react before the storm hit.

"Looked across, and I saw dark clouds and I saw a bunch of white. I said that looks like a lot of birds, and I went and got closer, I'm like, that's not birds, that's debris. And tried to hustle my dogs into my bedroom so we could all take cover," Christiansen said. He immediately took cover with his family and pets, and moments later found significant damage in his backyard.

Christiansen's patio furniture was submerged in his pool, his pool fence was blown toward his home, debris was scattered across the ground and plants were blown away. He received the emergency alert after the storm had already hit. Christiansen, originally from Minnesota, said his experience with tornado-like weather helped him know what precautions to take. He and his family and pets were not injured. Christiansen said he plans to have his roof inspected.
cards.headline: Port St. Lucie residents clean up after possible tornado strikes Southbend neighborhood
cards.teaser: Aaron Christiansen had about 10 seconds to take cover Sunday evening when he spotted debris swirling outside his window near Southbend Boulevard and Southeast Navy Ave. He and other residents began cleanup efforts Monday after the possible tornado or landspout damaged homes and yards.

hero.body:
The National Weather Service confirmed Monday that an EF0 tornado touched down Sunday evening in St. Lucie County, tracking 2.1 miles and damaging 20 to 30 homes with winds of 65 to 75 mph. Will Ulrich, warning coordination meteorologist with the National Weather Service Melbourne office, announced the findings during a press conference at Jessica Clinton Park following a damage survey of the affected areas. No injuries were reported from the tornado.

The tornado, classified as a landspout, first touched down around 6:10 p.m. near Southeast Kitching Cove Lane and Southeast Morningside Boulevard, close to the Tarpon Bay Yacht Club. The tornado produced minimal structural damage, including roof damage, soffit damage and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations. It then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout for approximately five to seven minutes, meandering slowly from north to south over the water before moving back onshore in the Bay St. Lucie community around 6:20 p.m.

The strongest wind gusts occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, Ulrich said, where the tornado caused numerous downed trees and large branches, along with damage to well-built homes with tile roofs. The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, where it caused discontinuous damage including downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. The entire event lasted approximately 14 to 15 minutes. Approximately 20 to 30 percent of roof covers were removed from some homes, though no homes were destroyed.

Ulrich explained that landspouts form differently than traditional tornadoes, developing closer to the surface along the leading edge of thunderstorm updrafts rather than from mesocyclones. Residents reported it was not raining during the tornado itself, with heavy rain arriving only after the tornado passed through. Ulrich said the tornado resulted from boundary interactions from daily afternoon showers and thunderstorms, noting that abnormally warm conditions create more vigorous boundary collisions. The National Weather Service worked alongside the City of Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct interviews with residents and piece together the timeline of the event.
hero.headline: National Weather Service confirms EF0 tornado tracked 2.1 miles through St. Lucie County

It produced minimal structural damage, including roof damage, soffit damage and pool enclosures lifted from their foundations. The tornado then moved over the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout for approximately five to seven minutes, meandering slowly from north to south over the water before moving back onshore in the Bay St. Lucie community around 6:20 p.m.

The strongest wind gusts likely occurred in the Bay St. Lucie community, where the tornado caused numerous downed trees and large branches, along with damage to well-built homes with tile roofs from winds of 65 to 75 mph. The tornado continued west into Port St. Lucie communities near the Southbend area, where it caused discontinuous damage including downed trees, blown-over fences, and damaged or destroyed pool screen enclosures before dissipating. The entire event lasted approximately 14 to 15 minutes, making it unusually long for this type of tornado. Most of the damage was classified as minor, with approximately 20 to 30 percent of roof covers removed from some homes, though no homes were destroyed.

No injuries were reported from the tornado. Residents reported it wasn't raining during the tornado itself, with heavy rain arriving only after the tornado passed through. The National Weather Service worked alongside the City of Port St. Lucie Emergency Management and St. Lucie County Emergency Management to conduct interviews with residents and piece together the timeline of the event.
